messages:
ops-bot: Paging @sre oncall: multiple nodes in cluster 'infer-prod-us-west' are reporting repeated Xid 13 / ECC correctable spikes and CUDA driver resets over the last 4m. Affected hosts: gpu-node-17,gpu-node-18,gpu-node-21. Auto-evac attempts started. :rotating_light:

ops-bot: summary: 17 driver resets, 6 pods restarted, OOMs observed in kvcache on gpu-node-21. Investigate and coordinate mitigation.

sre-alyssa: here — ack. I'm oncall. pulling logs now. tagging @eng-runtime-maya for driver's perspective.

oncall-ryan: I'm around too. quick check: are customer-facing endpoints degraded?

beth-cs: FYI we've seen 3 customer sessions drop in the last 5m, customers: acme-inc (prod), greenloop. They're opening tickets. Can we confirm scope?

kubebot: gpu-node-21: pods in namespace redwood-serving show CrashLoopBackOff: 6 restarts in 2m. Evacuation job created: evac-2026-03-15-01.

sre-alyssa: logs from gpu-node-21 dmesg tail:
```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:03:00): 13, PID=11223
[ 12345.679012] nvidia: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 12345.679123] kernel: nvidia-nvlink error
[ 12346.001234] oom_kill: cgroup_v1: memory force killed  pid=11292
```

sre-alyssa: also `kubectl top node gpu-node-21` shows memory pressure on GPU and host memory near 92%.

eng-runtime-maya: reading telemetry — we've seen an Xid 13 burst pattern which often indicates ECC or firmware noise. Not seeing metric for temp spike. Can you share `nvidia-smi --query` snapshot?

sre-alyssa: pasted nvidia-smi output snippet:
```
GPU 0: 55C, 98 % memory, Processes: 5
GPU 1: 54C, 91 % memory, Processes: 4
Persistence-M: Enabled
Attached GPUs: 2
```

eng-runtime-maya: thanks. this is a kvcache OOM waterfall — KV cache growth + driver resets -> containers restart -> cache rebuild -> more memory -> repeat. Short term: we should cordon gpu-node-21 and live-migrate running pods to nodes with headroom. Longer: need to throttle KV cache growth and patch driver if correlated.

infra-tom: cordon + drain sounds good. Note: gpu-node-17/18 are showing intermittent resets but not full OOM yet. I'll stage cordon for gpu-node-21 now.

oncall-ryan: do safe-drain with `--grace-period=60 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`? We should avoid killing long-running inferences midstream if possible.

eng-runtime-maya: recommend `kubectl drain gpu-node-21 --pod-selector='app!=realtime-session'` to preserve active realtime sessions. Then we can fallback their traffic to dedicated fallback model on dedicated capacity. We have routing policy that will use fallback if node unavailable.

beth-cs: can we put impacted customer sessions on dedicated fallback? acme-inc is on a reserved plan so priority routing is allowed. If you're switching them, tell me so we can message support.

sre-alyssa: infra-tom, go ahead with selective drain. I'll start a focused telemetry capture (nvidia-smi --query-gpu and kernel OOPS + driver logs) and upload to the incident channel.

infra-tom: running selective drain now. output:
```
cordon node/gpu-node-21
warning: ignoring DaemonSet-managed pods: kube-system/nv-agent
evicting pod redwood-serving/session-abc123 -> success
evicting pod redwood-serving/worker-xyz789 -> success
```

deploy-bot: noticed a model rollout in prod (release/rls-1.14) started ~18m ago. No direct errors in rollout, but pods targeted at gpu-node-21 have restarted. Tagging @eng-runtime-maya.

eng-runtime-maya: thanks @deploy-bot. Rollout paused for nodes with restarts. We should avoid re-scheduling the same heavy job to the remaining stressed nodes. I'll add a soft anti-affinity for the rollout to avoid the 3 nodes under pressure.

sre-alyssa: quick customer impact assessment: acme-inc had 2 requests dropped and one error 502. greenloop reported degraded latency (~2.1s -> ~5s) for embeddings. No P0s yet. Beth, recommend we open an incident update for customers in 30m unless things worsen.

eng-runtime-maya: mitigation checklist I'm running through:
- throttle kv cache growth (orch config): `REDWOOD_KV_MAX_BYTES=4g` on node to temporarily limit cache
- disable prefetch for suspect models
- increase driver persistence timeout (only if safe)
- coordinate controlled reboot if node continues to reset

sre-alyssa: applied KV cap to kube deployment for cached workers on gpu-node-21 via emergency patch. Monitoring memory.

ops-bot: telemetry: driver resets dropped from ~6/min to ~1/min after drain started and KV cap applied. Still seeing occasional Xid 13 on gpu-node-17.

eng-runtime-maya: that's promising. For gpu-node-17 we'll schedule a quick cordon + reboot during a maintenance window unless resets stop. For immediate, I'll push a kernel param tweak to reduce aggressive reclaim pressure.

infra-tom: creating a maintenance ticket to schedule a rolling reboot for nodes 17/18/21. ETA 45m.

beth-cs: We'll draft a customer-facing update: short note about transient GPU driver instability impacting some inference requests; workaround in place; we're investigating root cause and will update in 1h. Affected customers list: acme-inc, greenloop, beta-labs.

oncall-ryan: final ask before handoff: set incident priority (we have multiple paying customers affected) -> sev2 for now. If more than 10% of capacity impacted escalate to sev1.

sre-alyssa: agreed. I'm handing off to @eng-runtime-maya for follow-up on root cause analysis and driver patch coordination. I'll remain available for oncall if it flares.

eng-runtime-maya: taking over. I'll coordinate with drivers-eng and firmware team if telemetry points to ECC or microcode. Starting an RCA timeline doc.

ops-bot: incident ticket #INC-2026-045 created, status: active, lead: eng-runtime-maya, severity: sev2.

sre-alyssa: thanks team. moving to monitoring-only. keep this thread updated with any regressions. :white_check_mark:

eng-runtime-maya: copy — will post RCA notes and timeline here.

beth-cs: adding customer update draft to the ticket.

kubebot: node/gpu-node-21 marked unschedulable. evac job complete.

ops-bot: last_snapshot: driver_reset_rate=0.8/min, kvcache_rebuilds=2/min, errors still sporadic. Monitoring continues.
